meta.sub: Follow the sequence without losing connection

meta.sub: Stop contamination reaching the next child

practice.q: A child says “No” and pulls away. Nobody is in immediate danger. What is the best next step?
o: Hold the child still so care ends quickly.
Pause safely, reassure and seek support for timely care.
Leave the child soiled until collection.
practice.why: Care must be responsive and timely. Neither force for convenience nor abandoning necessary care is appropriate.

practice.q: What must be ready before routine care begins?
o: Only the school’s approved paper or digital care record.
The child’s arrangements, trained staff, supervision, privacy, supplies and a safe station.
practice.why: Preparation covers the child, people and environment. Missing resources must not lead to leaving a child unsafe.

o: Only items within the dirty part of the task, until safe removal and the approved clean transition.
The clean nappy packet if you are careful.
The care record, pen or recording device so the record is not forgotten.
practice.why: Keep contamination away from clean supplies, shared touchpoints and records. Use hand hygiene and maintain supervision during the transition.

practice.q: Which cleaning instructions should you follow after a change?
o: The school’s current approved local procedure and product directions.
A chemical recipe suggested by a colleague.
practice.why: Use the school’s approved routine and product directions. Ask the responsible lead if you are unsure; never improvise products, mixtures or contact times.

practice.q: The consent form names a different cream from the one in the child’s bag. What should happen?
o: Check and resolve permission for the exact product before applying it.
practice.why: Cream identity, consent and the medicine process where relevant must be checked; continue safe authorised care and obtain advice.

practice.q: What does a pass on this online course demonstrate?
o: Online requirements have been met; practical competence needs a separate observed check.
Automatic authorisation for independent intimate-care duties.
Qualification to carry out specialist medical procedures.
practice.why: Knowledge and reflections do not establish practical competence with the school’s equipment, procedures or individual care plans.

declarations: I understand that dignity, reassurance, appropriate privacy and continuous safe supervision are essential during intimate care.
I will work within my role, training, the child’s agreed arrangements and the school’s current approved procedures; I will seek help when I cannot do so safely.
I understand that force for convenience, humiliation and leaving necessary care unmet are unacceptable responses to distress.
I will follow the approved hand-hygiene, PPE, cleaning, product, cream/medication and waste procedures, and report gaps rather than improvise.
I will record facts and report concerns promptly through the confirmed safeguarding or staff-concern route, using independent escalation where required.
I understand that the certificate records online completion only. I still need the school’s required induction and a separate trained observer’s practical signoff before independent duties.

localReadiness.title: Current school procedure
localReadiness.text: Know where to find the school’s current approved intimate-care procedure and who to ask if anything is unclear.

localReadiness.title: Your role and training
localReadiness.text: Know which care tasks you are authorised and trained to carry out, who supervises you and when to ask for trained help.

localReadiness.title: Child plans and family agreements
localReadiness.text: Check where to find each child’s current care plan, communication needs, allergies and product permissions. Follow the approved arrangements for changes or extra care.

localReadiness.title: Privacy, layout and staffing
localReadiness.text: Use the designated care area and approved screening. Keep a colleague informed, follow the no-closed-door arrangement and maintain the required child and group supervision.

localReadiness.title: Safe access and continuous supervision
localReadiness.text: Know how to use the station safely, maintain supervision and call for help. Ask for a demonstration if you are unsure about equipment, moving a child or hand hygiene during care.

localReadiness.title: Hand hygiene and PPE
localReadiness.text: Follow the demonstrated handwashing, glove-change and apron routine. Know what to do if supplies run out, equipment is unsuitable or contamination occurs.

localReadiness.title: Cleaning products and contact time
localReadiness.text: Use only approved products and follow their directions, including contact time, drying or rinsing, protective equipment and safe storage. Ask the responsible lead if you are unsure. Never mix chemicals or use an unlabelled container.

localReadiness.title: Waste, laundry and equipment
localReadiness.text: Use the school’s approved bins, laundry and soiled-clothing arrangements. Keep waste away from children and clean supplies. Report full bins, damaged mats or missing equipment.

localReadiness.title: Creams and medicines
localReadiness.text: Check the child’s own labelled product, consent, directions and expiry date and permitted use after opening. Follow the separate medication process for prescribed creams; only authorised, trained staff may apply them.

localReadiness.title: Records, reporting and urgent help
localReadiness.text: Know the school’s approved paper or digital recording method, secure storage and family communication channel. Know your DSL, deputy and leadership contacts, including an independent route if a leader is involved, and how to get urgent help.

localReadiness.title: Your practical observation
localReadiness.text: Arrange the separate practical observation with an authorised school observer. Ask what supervised practice or further support you need before independent care.

practical.title: Separate school practical observation checklist
practical.intro: For use by an authorised, trained observer after local induction. This is a school-controlled practice record, separate from the online certificate. The participant must not award or self-sign practical competence.
instructions: Complete the local readiness checks first. Record the participant, school, observer’s role, observation date, policy version, setting/equipment and scope of the observation in the school’s approved record.

Demonstrate unfamiliar equipment and practise the sequence with suitable training materials before any care involving a child. Observe real care only when necessary, authorised and appropriate to the child’s plan; protect dignity and avoid unnecessary observers.

Use “Observed safely”, “Further support needed” or “Not observed” for each criterion and add factual evidence. Never use an intimate photograph or recording as evidence. Keep real children’s identities and care information out of course responses and downloadable training records.

Stop unsafe practice immediately while preserving the child’s safety and arrange appropriate support. A serious safety gap cannot be offset by strengths elsewhere. Record support, retraining and reassessment needed.

Only the authorised school observer can recommend signoff for the scope actually observed. The responsible school leader confirms authorisation under local policy. A blank or unobserved item does not count as a pass.

items: Confirms role permissions, local induction and the current child’s arrangements before beginning.
Identifies how to summon help and confirms who is supervising other children.
Recognises tasks, equipment or medicine administration outside their competence and seeks the right support.
Explains steps in accessible language and responds to the child’s words and non-verbal cues.
Encourages manageable independence and offers genuine choices without pressure or shaming.
Uses approved screening and colleague-awareness arrangements while meeting the no-closed-door requirement.
Responds to distress with a safe pause, reassurance and a supported plan for timely care; does not use force for convenience.
Checks the surface and equipment and prepares the correct clean supplies, PPE and waste arrangement.
Keeps chemicals, bags and unsafe items inaccessible to children and clean stock away from contamination.

Uses only the demonstrated safe access/transfer method and maintains active supervision throughout, including the protective contact and positioning demonstrated locally to prevent falls from a raised surface.
Demonstrates a safe response to a missing item without leaving a child unattended.
Performs the locally required hand hygiene and uses fresh approved PPE for each change.
Explains and carries out the locally demonstrated cleaning and changing sequence gently and within the care plan.
Contains soiling and protects clean supplies and touchpoints from contaminated gloves.
Removes contaminated gloves safely and performs the approved hand-hygiene/clean-care transition while preserving supervision.
Checks exact cream permissions and uses a clean application method without cross-contaminating containers.
Supports child handwashing and dressing and confirms safe supervision before station cleaning.
Uses the approved cleaning/disinfection procedure, correct product and label contact time, including drying/rinsing where required.
Deals with contaminated touchpoints, waste and soiled clothing through the approved route.
Removes cleaning PPE, washes and dries hands and returns the station to a safe ready state.
Knows how to manage a spill, exposure, product shortage or damaged surface and obtain help.
Completes an accurate, discreet care record and appropriate routine handover.
Explains how to report a child concern and a staff-conduct concern without diagnosing or investigating.
Identifies the confirmed deputy/alternative, independent leadership route and response to an unacknowledged report.
Explains the limits of online completion and the next steps if further practice or training is needed.

decisionOptions: Observed safely within the stated scope; school authorisation to be confirmed
Further supported practice and reassessment required
practical.footer: Record the observer’s evidence, scope, decision, support plan, reassessment date and signatures in the approved school system. Keep the record secure. This checklist does not replace the school’s policy, professional judgement or any required specialist qualification.

visualGuides.title: Prepare before you begin
visualGuides.intro: A short abstract station-planning guide. It does not demonstrate lifting, positioning or intimate physical care.

steps.title: Check the plan
steps.text: Confirm the child’s arrangements, your role and any product permission.

steps.title: Agree supervision
steps.text: A colleague knows care is happening; the group is covered and help can be called.

steps.title: Ready the station
steps.text: Check the surface and prepare clean supplies, fresh PPE, handwashing and waste.

steps.title: Protect the boundaries
steps.text: Keep clean stock separate from care and waste; keep bags and chemicals out of reach.

steps.title: Reassure and begin
steps.text: Explain the next step. Begin only when privacy, safety and the approved routine are ready.

visualGuides.transcript: Before the child comes to the station, check their care arrangements and your role. Tell the appropriate colleague and confirm supervision for the group. Make sure you can call for help. Check the surface, prepare the correct supplies and locate the handwashing and waste facilities. Keep clean stock separate from the changing and waste areas, and keep bags and chemicals out of reach. Plan how hand hygiene can happen without leaving the child unsafe. Check privacy screening. Explain the next step warmly and give the child time to respond. If something essential is missing, resolve it before routine care starts.

visualGuides.title: Keep clean and dirty apart
visualGuides.intro: Follow the movement of contamination through an abstract sequence. Learn the exact technique at your school’s practical demonstration.

steps.title: Begin clean
steps.text: Prepare supplies and perform hand hygiene before fresh PPE and care.

steps.title: Contain the dirty phase
steps.text: Keep soiled nappies, wipes and clothing away from clean stock.

steps.title: Stop at the boundary
steps.text: Dirty gloves must not touch clean supplies, handles, cream containers or records.

steps.title: Make the clean transition
steps.text: Follow safe glove removal and the approved hand-hygiene sequence while supervising the child.

steps.title: Finish, then reset
steps.text: Support child handwashing, confirm safe supervision, clean the station and wash your hands.

visualGuides.transcript: Think of the routine as a clean area, a care area and contained waste. Begin with prepared supplies and hand hygiene. During the dirty part, keep soiling and used materials away from clean stock. Stop before your contaminated gloves touch a nappy packet, cream container, care record, pen, recording device or door handle. Follow the school’s demonstrated glove-removal and hand-hygiene sequence, with the child safely supervised at every moment. Ask for trained help if needed. Complete clean care and support the child’s handwashing. Confirm they are in a safe, supervised place before resetting the station. Finish with the required PPE removal and handwashing.

visualGuides.title: Reassure a worried child
visualGuides.intro: A communication example with abstract characters and speech bubbles. No intimate bodies or hands-on restraint are depicted.

steps.title: Notice
steps.text: The child pulls away. Treat this as a cue to pause and understand their needs.

steps.title: Pause safely
steps.text: Keep the child safe and say: “We can pause. I can see you are worried.”

steps.title: Offer a real choice
steps.text: “Would you like to help with your clothes, or would you like Sam to help?”

steps.title: Get familiar support
steps.text: Call a trained colleague without leaving the child unsafe. Follow the care plan.

steps.title: Plan timely care
steps.text: Do not force for convenience or abandon care. Obtain advice if distress or pain continues.

visualGuides.transcript: A child pulls away and says no. Pause where it is safe and keep your voice calm. You might say, “We can pause. I can see you are worried.” Explain the next small step and offer a genuine choice, such as helping with clothing or having a familiar trained adult assist. Give the child time to communicate. Call for support without leaving them unsafe, and use their agreed plan. Do not hold them down to save time. A pause must lead to timely, respectful care. If distress or pain continues, obtain appropriate advice and report any concern through the school’s process.
